item.title: Robot reaches 4,500-year-old sealed barrier inside Egypt’s Great Pyramid
item.description: A robot explored a hidden passage within Egypt's Great Pyramid of Giza. It reached a sealed barrier which may be 4,500 years old. This discovery has renewed questions about the ancient monument's hidden contents. Researchers used modern technology to examine areas difficult for people to access. Further study could reveal new details about the pyramid's design and construction.

item.title: UP polls: How parties are vying for Dalit votes amid Mayawati’s shrinking base
item.description: A notable evolution in Dalit politics is unfolding in Uttar Pradesh, marked by a decline in the Bahujan Samaj Party's dominance. The Bharatiya Janata Party and the Samajwadi Party are actively courting Dalit voters ahead of elections, and the Congress party is also working to regain its historic connections. Meanwhile, Chandrashekhar Azad is establishing a distinct political identity, foreshadowing a significant shift in the Dalit electoral landscape.
item.dc:creator: PRIYANKA MUKHERJEE

item.title: 'No clear info': Nepal PM claims Indian territory, but 'loses' 210-year-old treaty papers
item.description: Nepal's foreign minister announced that the country might have misplaced the original Sugauli Treaty papers, which played a critical role in establishing its borders with British India after the Anglo-Nepalese War. This comes at a time when border disputes with India have intensified. The government plans to systematically assess numerous international agreements, seeking to amend or renew any that are no longer pertinent.
item.dc:creator: TOI NEWS DESK

item.title: Months after Dells' $6.25bn ‘gift’, US Treasury sets new Trump Account paycheck rules
item.description: Under the new guidelines for Trump Accounts, both employers and employees can make contributions towards payrolls. Employers are permitted to add up to $2,500 annually without tax for dependent children, while employees can contribute pre-tax funds directly from their paychecks. In support of this initiative, Michael and Susan Dell committed $6.25 billion to boost child savings. The proposal is currently open for public feedback prior to its finalization.

item.title: Deepwater Horizon damaged deep-sea corals; NOAA is now planting new colonies
item.description: In a groundbreaking initiative, scientists are working to revive deep-sea coral ecosystems that were harmed by an oil spill. Utilizing corals grown in laboratories along with advanced tools, they have successfully deployed these corals at great depths. This project focuses on rejuvenating delicate habitats in the Gulf of Mexico, with ongoing monitoring set to evaluate both the survival rates of the corals and the overall restoration of the ecosystem.
item.dc:creator: TOI SCIENCE DESK

item.title: In 1929, Tennessee farmer refused $20 an acre, then lost his farm
item.description: In 1929, Tennessee farmer John W. Oliver refused to sell his 375-acre Cades Cove farm for $20 an acre, leading to a lengthy court battle over land wanted for Great Smoky Mountains National Park. After the Tennessee Supreme Court ruled against him, Oliver ultimately lost his property and received $17,000 in 1935.

item.title: Google co-founder’s message for DeepMind staff after Demis Hassabis exits as CEO
item.description: Google co-founder Sergey Brin has been urging Google DeepMind staff to go all in on Gemini and catch up to the AI frontier, following a sweeping leadership overhaul that saw Demis Hassabis step aside as CEO. Koray Kavukcuoglu now runs day-to-day operations from Mountain View, with final say on major decisions. The reshuffle follows Gemini release delays, coding benchmark gaps against Anthropic and OpenAI, and high-profile exits including Jeff Dean.

item.title: Who was Jessica Bang? Rising golf star dies at 18 after brain hemorrhage
item.description: In a heartbreaking incident, eighteen-year-old Jessica Bang, an up-and-coming Australian golfer, died in Thailand due to a brain hemorrhage while training for a key tournament. After collapsing and requiring emergency surgery, she sadly passed away. Her family has initiated a fundraiser to cover medical expenses and facilitate her return home. The loss of such a talented athlete has left the Australian golf community in deep sorrow.

item.title: She was just 3km from home: B'luru keeps fixing roads, yet they keep turning deadly
item.description: The tragic accident involving Medha Akarsh underscores the ongoing road infrastructure challenges in Bengaluru. Despite ongoing attempts to repair the extensive pothole issue, the roads are frequently excavated for utility repairs, leading to further damage. This troubling cycle poses daily risks to commuters, emphasizing the urgent need for better coordination and accountability in road maintenance and safety measures.

item.title: Hours after ban, BCI reverses decision on NALSAR 2026 batch over CJI invite row
item.description: The Bar Council of India has revised its previous directive concerning NALSAR graduates. Students from NALSAR's 2026 cohort can now pursue enrollment with state bar councils. This update followed significant backlash against the original ruling, which prevented these students from becoming advocates due to their association with a protest. The regulator emphasized that the majority of the students were uninvolved and innocent.

item.title: The real cost of a govt exam: Years, money, age & a future postponed
item.description: Students in Ranchi are protesting alleged irregularities in government examinations for 20 days. Seven students are on hunger strike, with three hospitalized due to failing health. They demand the chief minister meet them to discuss their concerns directly. Years of exam delays and age limit issues fuel widespread aspirant frustration across India. This ongoing uncertainty impacts career choices and mental well-being for many young individuals.

item.title: American mom who had daughter at 18 helps her reach dream college 18 years later
item.description: Against the odds of poverty, Jeanice Perez worked tirelessly to provide her daughter Jordyn with the educational opportunities she never had. Her meticulous savings paved the way for Jordyn's ambitious goal of studying biology at New York University. Jeanice proudly reflects on their strong, nurturing relationship as her most significant achievement, showing that young motherhood can lead to a brilliant future.

item.title: CAG finds 98% shortfall in Green India Mission forest cover targets, flags lapses
item.description: The Comptroller and Auditor General raised concerns about the inadequacies within the Green India Mission program, noting that the goal of increasing forest cover was far from realized over a decade. The audit pointed to significant issues in planning and financial oversight, which severely undermined the mission's objectives. Key vulnerable areas were neglected during afforestation, diminishing efforts to combat climate change.
item.dc:creator: VISHWA MOHAN

item.title: Elizabeth Taylor’s former Bel Air estate gets $47m makeover - What is the plan
item.description: The legendary Bel Air residence of Elizabeth Taylor is undergoing a stunning renovation led by developer Ardie Tavangarian. Aiming to celebrate and retain the actress's memorable essence, the project will merge the original home with an impressive modern addition. Key areas, including Taylor's iconic master bedroom, are being meticulously restored and updated. This remarkable transformation is set for completion next year, promising a breathtaking homage to the star's legacy.

item.title: Sri Lankan coach dies after altercation with cricketer in Colombo
item.description: Tragic news strikes the cricket community as veteran coach Sumith Fernando passes away at 62 following a violent altercation. The incident, which took place on August 8 at a Colombo cricket facility, started over a dispute regarding drinking water. A 17-year-old player has been arrested in connection with this troubling event. Fernando was well-known for his role in mentoring Sri Lanka's ODI captain, Kusal Mendis.

The initiative, spearheaded by state governments with central technical assistance, is aligned with the National Critical Mineral Mission aimed at bolstering self-reliance. This move is crucial in propelling India’s transition toward green energy, ensuring a sustainable future.

item.description: Aaradhya Bachchan filed a Delhi High Court case against fake online information. The court is examining if family reputation can be treated like a trademark. It will also consider if fake news violates intellectual property rights. The case explores defamation within intellectual property law frameworks.
